name: Hare
idea: A walker that runs. Same six spoked legs as the league, but a light frame, full-size motors and a gait driven at more than twice the league's pace, with a steel lance held out ahead. It strikes at a run, where a blow breaks joints, and is gone before the enemy has turned.

name: Lever
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Warden, Mantis), including the champion.
idea: Win the shoving match by taking the enemy's weight. A heavy wheeled machine slides a steel fork under the enemy and lifts: the enemy's feet lose their grip, that weight lands on this machine's front wheels, and it carries the enemy to the edge. Nothing in the league lifts.

name: Wasp
idea: Speed as the weapon. A 430 kg wheeled wedge that goes three times as fast as anything in the league, hits the enemy on the side facing away from the nearest edge, and if the enemy does not give, pulls out and comes again from a new angle instead of leaning on it.

name: Bolt
idea: Wasp from round 1 rebuilt for a small ring, where there is no room to reach top speed: six wheels on full-size motors for pull-away, thick steel axles, and runs that start from seven metres out. A wheeled wedge that hits the enemy on the side facing away from the nearest edge, and if the enemy does not give, pulls out and comes again from a new angle instead of leaning on it.

name: Jab
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Dreadnought, Strider), including the champion.
idea: A boxer that goes for the legs. Every machine in the league stands on spoked legs whose joints are its weakest, and a blow counts by how fast it lands, so this machine carries three piston fists that strike at 8 m/s whatever its own speed. It picks the nearest leg still attached, sets itself at exactly fist range from it, jabs, and steps back out of reach while the fists recharge.

name: Jack
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Dreadnought), including the champion.
idea: Lever from round 1 with the two faults its fights showed put right: axles of thick steel, since Lever lost two of three just landing on rough ground, and a fork that stays under the enemy and keeps carrying instead of letting go after four seconds. Win the shoving match by taking the enemy's weight. A heavy wheeled machine slides a steel fork under the enemy and lifts: the enemy's feet lose their grip, that weight lands on this machine's front wheels, and it carries the enemy to the edge. Nothing in the league lifts.

name: Sparrer
why: Knocked out by Jab in 36.8 s (ring_out).
idea: Jab on legs. Jab's wheels stalled on the hills and it drew two of its four fights standing off. This puts the same three piston fists and the same leg-picking program on the league's six-legged steel frame, to see whether the boxer works on ground that wheels cannot take.

name: Toss
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Jab, Warden), including the champion.
idea: A flipper, to end the draws. Thick-steel machines shrug off every blow in the league, so this one does not try to break them: it slides three steel pads under the enemy and fires them upward together on geared pistons, 30 kN in all, enough to throw a 700 kg machine off its feet. Then it drives the tumbling machine out before it recovers.
